Package lan.sdi.usb2iic.pololu.impl

Class USB_I2C_BridgeImpl

  • java.lang.Object
    • lan.sdi.usb2iic.pololu.impl.USB_I2C_BridgeImpl
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    USB_I2C_Bridge
    public class USB_I2C_BridgeImpl
extends java.lang.Object
implements USB_I2C_Bridge
    Responsibilities:
    • Search for the Pololu USB 2 I2C adaptor in the device list of the host system
    • Initialize the Pololu USB to I2C adaptor
    • Do I2C read / write and administrative operations
    • Provide I2C error information
    • Provide access to the jSerialCom status and error information

    Collaborators:
    jSerialCom.SerialPort

    Description:
    USB_I2C_BridgeImpl acts as bridge between two worlds: The USB interface on a PC and the I2C interface with I2C devices connected to it.
    It provides easy read, write and write/read access to the connected I2C devices.

    Some operations return a U2iResponse object which contains the status of the invoked operation. T least, the field errorCode should be checked to verify that the operation was successful.
    If the errorCode is not 0, the getLastError() should be invoked to obtain error information of the serial underlying interface.

    For detailed information, please refer to the vendors documentation. Command reference

    Author:
    Stefan

      • close

        public boolean close()
        Perform a close operation on the underlying serial port.

        This command must be send to the USB to I2C bridge before the host application terminates.
        Otherwise, the related COM port stays in a undefined state and can't be re-opened.

        Specified by:
        close in interface USB_I2C_Bridge

      • digitalRead

        public byte digitalRead()
                 throws USB_I2C_Exception
        This command retrieves digital readings of the adapterâ€™s internal SCL and SDA signals, which can be useful for troubleshooting.

        Normally the bus will be idle when the adapter executes this command, so both readings will be high (1).
        If the SDA reading is low (0), the Clear bus command might restore your bus to a working state.

        Specified by:
        digitalRead in interface USB_I2C_Bridge
        Returns:
        A byte: bit 0 represents SCL, bit 1 represents SDA state.
        Throws:
        USB_I2C_Exception - If either writing the command byte or reading the bus status is impossible.

        Call the getLastError() method to obtain detailed informations about the error.

        USB_I2C_Exception - If either the write command or read data command fails.

      • i2cRead

        public U2iResponse i2cRead​(int aAddress,
                           byte[] aBuffer)
        Read aBuffer.length bytes from the I2C device with address aAddress.
        The data read are placed in the given buffer. Furthermore a U2iResponse object is set up with the status informations of the command execution.

        The U2iResponse object must be checked to determine whether the operation was successful or not.

        Specified by:
        i2cRead in interface USB_I2C_Bridge
        Parameters:
        aAddress - The 7-bit I2C address of the device to read from.
        aBuffer - A byte array large enough to hold the data to be read.
        Returns:
        U2iResponse holding the status information of this operation.

      • i2cWriteRead

        public U2iResponse i2cWriteRead​(int aAddress,
                                byte[] aWriteBuffer,
                                byte[] aReadBuffer)
        Performs a w/r operation on the I2C bus with a repeated start condition.

        First, aWriteBuffer.length bytes are read from aWriteBuffer and written to the I2C device with the address aAddress.
        Then, a read operation is performed to read aReadBuffer.length bytes from the addresses device. The bytes read are placed in aReadBuffer.

        Specified by:
        i2cWriteRead in interface USB_I2C_Bridge
        Parameters:
        aAddress - The 7-bit I2C address of the device to write to.
        aWriteBuffer - A byte array holding the data to be written.
        aReadBuffer - A byte array large enough to hold the data to be read.

      • i2cWriteRead

        public U2iResponse i2cWriteRead​(int aAddress,
                                byte[] aWriteBuffer,
                                int aWriteOffset,
                                int aWriteLength,
                                byte[] aReadBuffer,
                                int aReadOffset,
                                int aReadLength)
        Performs a w/r operation on the I2C bus with a repeated start condition.

        First, aWriteLength bytes are read from aWriteBuffer, starting at aWriteOffset and written to the I2C device with the address aAddress.
        Then, a read operation is performed to read aReadLength bytes from the addresses device. The bytes read are placed in aReadBuffer starting at aReadOffset.

        Specified by:
        i2cWriteRead in interface USB_I2C_Bridge
        Parameters:
        aAddress - The 7-bit I2C address of the device to write to.
        aWriteBuffer - A byte array holding the data to be written.
        aWriteOffset - The location where the first byte is read from the buffer.
        aWriteLength - Number of bytes to read from buffer and write to the addressed device.
        aReadBuffer - A byte array large enough to hold the data to be read.
        aReadOffset - Location, where the first byte read is placed in the buffer.
        aReadLength - Number of bytes to read from addressed device.

      • resetSerialPort

        public void resetSerialPort()
        If an communication error has occurred on the underlying serial port, which prevents further operation, a reset of the serial port might be helpful.

        With this command, a Break condition is send on the serial interface, causing the adaptor to reset and reinitialize it's serial port.

        Specified by:
        resetSerialPort in interface USB_I2C_Bridge

      • setI2cMode

        public U2iResponse setI2cMode​(I2C_MODE aMode)
        Set the operation mode for the I2C interface.

        Valid modes are (as defined in I2C_MODE):

        • I2C_MODE.STANDARD
        • I2C_MODE.FAST
        • I2C_MODE.FAST_PLUS
        • I2C_MODE.SLOW_10_KHZ (Pololu defined slow mode).
        Detailed information about the I2C bus modes can be obtained from IÂ²C-bus specification and user manual

        Specified by:
        setI2cMode in interface USB_I2C_Bridge
        Parameters:
        aMode - The desired operation mode.
        Please read the data sheets of the connected devices along with the I2C bus specification to choose the correct bus operation mode!

      • setI2cTimeout

        public U2iResponse setI2cTimeout​(int aTimeOut)
        This command sets the maximum time allowed for IÂ²C write and IÂ²C read commands.

        If the total time taken by IÂ²C communication in one of those commands takes longer than the specified time, the adapter aborts the command and returns the timeout error code (3).

        Specified by:
        setI2cTimeout in interface USB_I2C_Bridge
        Parameters:
        aTimeOut - A number of milliseconds from 1 to 65535.
        The default IÂ²C timeout is 50 ms.
